Last but not least, the soundtrack is phenomenal, so much so that I find myself listening to it when I'm not even playing the game. Even if you decide not to buy VVVVVV, do yourself a favor and listen to the soundtrack (titled "PPPPPP") on your streaming platform of choice.

I really enjoyed "The Crew" and its downloadable contents, mainly for its great open world—the reproduction of the whole United States in a smaller version.
Every time I play the game, I am surprised how detailed the environment and the cities really are.
Although there are game objects (like houses in small towns around the world map) which do actually appear quite often, it still is fascinating how many different buildings and environmental structures (deserts, mountains, snow landscapes) there are and how it affects the playstyle, giving the player various opportunities to enjoy the game in very different ways.
The car selection in the game is good, all in all. If you want great cars however, you almost have to spend real money on as The Crew's in-game currency adds up extremely slowly.
The multiplayer functionalitites of the game are fine overall. However, the game's genre would be more accurate without the "Massive" in "Massively Multiplayer Online Game". Most of the players on your map are multiple kilometers/miles away from you, but when finding one, it is really fun to drive around with the other player. Also, one thing to criticize is the game's always-online "feature". Playing the game when the servers are offline, which happens quite frequently, is impossible. I would like it even more if there was an offline mode, making it possible to play alone and without any active online connection.
Moving on to the game's story, it is basically like in any other MMO-type racing game. Without spoiling its contents: Not too interesting, but kind of okay. You get phone calls from different people, have to drive to a specific point on a map and have to clear a specific mission. That's it.
Ubisoft's DLC policy for The Crew (unlike any other of this publisher's games) is now kind of fair. You get the game for a pretty low price and the two major DLC packages (Calling all Units, including Wild Run) for a decent amount as well—compared to other games, at least. This however does not include all of the car packs, which are ridiculously expensive.
The two major DLCs for the game are pretty good, actually, as they add new game mechanics like bikes or even a completely new police mode.
Overall, I think that The Crew is a great game to get, mainly due to its open world features. But if you're looking for a racing game that completely focuses on the racing part, you probably want to get another game.
The term which would sum up what The Crew is like would probably be "Need for Speed, but with better online features and a more interesting map".

...And for far too many, it is where one ends, those invisible walls forever keeping them from venturing farther than the experiences of the past.
This is as advertised - a short, narrative, walking-simulator, yet that accurate description seems to not say enough. It's an emotive collection of memories we explore through the mind's eye of an adult narrator, reflecting on one morning in her youth, and the impactful types of events and thoughts that she has retained that have shaped her life.
It's reflective, peaceful, yet sad and thoughtful. I found myself wondering along with her about the things she ponders. Much of the experience is what the player will put into it - that's the interactive element for me, and this game is indeed like reading the "story" in a book, but with the visual and auditory elements too.
I'd like to know more of this narrator's other life chapters. But, another appeal for me is that this is a snapshot of a morning, where objects symbolise and spark memories, and a glimpse the narrator is sharing of herself. And maybe as just a glimpse, this experience works best.
Oh - I must comment on the music. It instantly set a mood for me, much as the piano pieces in, "Girl Interrupted" did - great soundtrack for this game.

game this is. Maybe it's less dismal with VR; I'm working with a mouse, so... ugh. (And yes, this is a thumbs-up review.) This is a reliving-childhood-memories game, with a style that makes it clear that most of those memories were miserable. However, it's distant, far-removed trauma, so it comes across as not so much angsty or even emo, but just mildly depressing.
It does have some bright spots, and those stand in sharp contrast to the majority of the story, even though they are obviously tiny fragments of the narrator's history, so that works well.
Gameplay mechanics are good, for the genre (I have no great love for VR-inspired games); the sounds are crisp and realistic and the graphics work well. There are a small number of things to figure out/do, but mostly this is explore-and-learn; It doesn't take long to explore everything.
It's well-made, and hauntingly memorable, but don't play it on the weekend you were looking for a pick-me-up; this isn't that. The most positive aspect of the story is the fact that the narrator obviously left her dismal beginnings far behind at some point.

I was as Moderator of a big German TW forum at SEGA in Munich / Germany when Napoleon TW was shown by Creative Assembly to the folks 2 weeks before release.
The game brought many features and improvements which were missing at Empire and which ... what I know for sure because confirmed later by a member of Creative Assembly ... were planned to give with Empire too. I'm not talking about the Multiplayer Campaign alone, but about things like the craters in batllefield, improved AI behavior in battle (slightly better as at Empire), more provinces as for example "Meckelnburg" north of Prussia or "Oldenburg" north of the Netherlands or "Hessen-Kassel" ... as well splitting France and Spain into more provinces. People asking why this was not done in Empire too get the correct answer that the game machine has problems to handle more provinces and factions as given ... and that's for example the reason why in North America is huge area with no province Between the East and the Plain Indians. Here in Napoleon the focus is only on Europe and so the map could be splitted into these further provinces and factions.
Also, other things like the Arsenals were in origin planned to give with Emipre too as well things which were introduced / changed by the Darth Mod in Empire were here at Napoleon given by Creative Assembly.
The game makes fun, no doubts ... as well it is again much improved by playing with Darth Mod. It is always interesting that the Greek modder Darth Vader and his team are no wizards here, but as still done at Empire, they change and improve existing things in the game "only" ... something what developers of Creative Assembly had to do by their own with proper testing in my opinion.
The historic battles and the way of Napoleon with Italian and Egypt campain are a good thing and well done as small level campain feature.
One change in the game done at battles is the sort of infantry fire with no fire by ranks etc. Take a closer look and scroll down in a battle to a unit and count who is only fires and make comparison to Empire. Another change is the splitting into 2 types of howitzers with different ammuniution, which I can't really understand why done with historic view on it, but also with gamers view.
Conclusion:
In general Napoleon is an improved Empire on Europe map only, officially justified by Creative Assembly that this war was on land only in Europe. This is histocally true, but the map of the main campaign should be something bigger by including the same area as Europe in Empire ... means complete Turkey, Palestine / Jordan / Syria, North Africa and in the west the sea area up (and including) Iceland ... as well complete Scandinavia. Pure by number of provinces and factions it ia fact that the game machine could handle without problems and so it is for me not understand able why Creative Assembly did not include.
The game itself wasn't so bugged as Empire at release and worked very good.
One point I can't forgive is some type of lie done by Creative Assembly here:
As part of the promotion of the game and clearly written in promotion text it was told that "modding tools" will be given. Sure, most players are casuals and so lesser interested in modding a game, no doubts, but when a company tells it in promotion to give, then it is to rate as promise. People who asked them after release when these "modding tools" will come and what they are able to change in game was not told much and if any official answer came it was only a short consoling. Some month later, the promotion text was over night changed and the part with the "modding tools" wassimply deleted without any comment or reaction when people like me asked them about it. Result: Which modding tools should be given can people ask now and CA could answer we never told! Fortunatelly I have a screenshot of the original text and even if these tools are not much worth in practice, this behavior of CA is not acceptable!

I spent ~430 hours on battlefield 1, and only 4 hours on Verdun at the time of writing those lines.
Well.
I love Verdun much more than Battlefield 1 one on those points:
* Gameplay: targets are hard to see, and you're not a bullet-magnet like in BF1. You mean lifetime on the ground is much higher than with Bf1. Also when you die, you know exactly why: it's because of you, and only you. Not because the game let players shoot you 1 sec after you spawn.
* Weapons: they are so great. Iron sight is hard and painful, as it would be in reality. Controlling your weapon is a challenge. No matter what weapon it is: rifle, pistol, nades, anything…
* Maps: trenches, holes in the ground, dirt, trees, grass, barbed wires, forts, holly **** we're in it!
* Pace: slower than BF1, but you can "speed up" the thing by increasing field of view to 70-80. Still, the game is slower but offers a real challeng on the battlefield… see what i did there? hehe
* Technical performance: the game does run really good, much more than BF1 in low. (i7 6700K + GTX 970). And you still have good graphics that adds to the game. The environment gives you countless ways to hide, sneak under the wires and all.
* Game modes: frontlines, deathmatch, battle-against-waves-oh-i-forgot-the-name. In frontlines mode, you'll have to play with your team. And it's awesome!
* Weapon and class system: more complex than BF1, but has more to offer than, especially because weapons are really different. For example, you take the Lebel, you have 8 bullets. You take the Berthier, you have 3 DESTROYING bullets. But you cannot reload while your charger has bullets left inside.
What i dislike about the game, but doesn't matter that much to me:
* Graphics are "oldschool": a bit too grey and "rigid". But this is also a plus since it makes you dive in the war.
* Sound design: awww… it hurts. It wouldn't matter if it was only weapon sounds. It's the way sound is rendered in space and how you can use the sound to get information about your environment. In my opinion, it can be improved.
* UI: small fonts, too much things displayed and i have no idea what's it's for.  But you can enjoy the game without that :)
For those who like that, the game offers levels that you grow while playing in a squad, giving you bonus while playing. I'm not so interested with this part of the game, but a friend i play with really loves it.
This game can and should be improved, still i recommend this game for all those players who wants challenging game and immersion into war. Not just random shots in the head from campers at the other side of the map.
This games is definitively a good game despites it's weak points.
100% recommended.

The Napoleon installment in the Total War franchise is, in my opinion, one of the best thus far. Compared to its predecessors, Napoleon TW boasts the best projectile combat for gunpowder based units (except for cannons). Line infantry, skirmishers, and snipers are all integrated effectively so that an armed comabt force can utilize all three of them without running into issues. Additionally, the balance of the game is quite good in that all units have counters and all counters have units that counter them. No one army can be used to defeat all counters. That being said, however, the game does have a few notable issues that detract from the enjoyability of the game. The first issue is that standard cannons have horrible trajectory algorithms. Cannons in Napoleon TW will consistently fire into the ground if they are not placed on flat ground or on a downward slope. This makes non-mortar artillery extremely frusterating to use since it is difficult to discern if the land you're deploying them on is 100% flat or if it is slightly rough. The second issue with the game is that melee combat is quite ackward due to a lack of proper unit collision in the game. As a result, units can be "pulled" through enemy lines by simply ordering units to run through the enemies. That being said, Napoleon TW is still a solid game and an excellent RTS. I recommend giving it a try.

If you enjoy games like Diablo, Torchlight, etc. this game is a must buy.

Divinity II has been my favorite western RPG of all time since its original release as Divinity II: Ego Draconis in 2009 (Skyrim is a close second). I just finished my first PC playthrough for the first time today (2/8/2017). Full Disclaimer: I own both Divinity II: Ego Draconis and Divinity II: Dragon Knight Saga for the Xbox 360 and have about 400 hours put into the both combined, and have beaten the game an estimated eleven times. My 30 hour gameplay is shorter than average and does not include the Flames of Vengeance game content. Most first time players can expect to get about 45-60 hours worth of content depending on character build, how many side quests you complete, etc.
Divinity II does something no other RPG has ever done to such a perfect extent: its main theme offers a duality of humor and depression, creating a juxtaposition not often found anywhere else. Throughout the first fifteen or so hours of the game, much of its humor shines through. Some of the most unique side quests found in RPGs of the era are thrown your way here, and choices are given to you as to how to treat the quest givers, what rewards you receive after a quest (pick XP, gold, potions, weapons, or sometimes even tableware, ha), or even how you complete a quest. You can decide whether your character is a kind hero, a♥♥♥♥♥♥talking ego-maniac, or something in-between, and sometimes this affects the outcomes of quests you partake. After the first fifteen in-game hours or so, the game opens up and reveals its simulation elements, allowing you to own your own battle tower and upgrade wings of it to better serve you (necromancy, alchemist, skills trainer, and weapon/armor enchanter). This will also be the part of the game that gives you the ability to turn into a dragon, something sorely missing in games of any genre, and it is aptly epic. You can level up your dragon abilities separate from your character abilities however you'd like, and you'll be able to reach places you couldn't before and even partake in some boss fights as a dragon. You are given multiple fortresses to take on however you'd like, utilizing both your human and dragon forms.
This is also the part of the game where you begin to see Divinity II's more depressing themes shine through. Evil is spreading through the land like a virus and it is up to you to stop it. Friends will become foe. Villages and people you've helped before will die, and quite tragically. Without spoiling anything, the game's ending is a punch in the gut and more memorable than any other game I've played yet; the game's ability to throw RPG "heroes make everything better and everything turns out okay" cliches into a fire pit is one to be admired. While the ending did make some people upset during the game's original release date, they updated it to "fix" it for fans with the Flames of Vengeance content. While I give kudos to them for being  people pleasers, I personally feel the creator's original intent is best. It is one of the reasons this game stands out to me above all others. While I have played the Flames of Vengeance content many times, I always play it separately; I like to think of the original game with its depressing and twisted ending as the full package, because it means a lot to me.
What are some flaws? Very few, but for one, the game was released in 2009, and its graphics are quite aged, as to be expected. I prefer graphics from the late '90s to mid '00s era to current, but most do not, so that's something to keep in mind. Also, the game is quite challenging when compared to others in the RPG genre. My husband (who is the reason I even found out about the game back in 2009, since he played the 360 demo) finds it too challenging and has never gotten farther than Sentinel Island. With quick reflexes and the changing of tactics, this should be no problem, however. (Also, it should be noted that the Developer's Cut PC edition is VASTLY easier than Ego Draconis from the 360, which is, in my opinion, a flaw. I preferred the challenge.) Lastly, the character models are so similar between every NPC, so while you meet many different characters, they do end up all looking like they're related.
Divinity II is a game I just can't stop playing. I play through it at least once a year because it offers so much that others in the genre simply don't. The soundtrack is my favorite of all time as well, even moreso than Journey, and I have a physical copy that I keep in my car. This game is the reason I became a fan of all things Larian, and while I am very happy at their success with Divinity: Original Sin and its sequel and have bought and played this game's predecessors (both here and on GOG), Divinity II will always be my favorite. There's just "something" about it. I love this game with a passion, and I highly recommend it to any fan of RPGs or to any fan of endings that aren't always cheesily happy. This is one of the few games I can in good conscience give a 10/10.

This game is an unappreciated gem of an action RPG. There's so many little thing about it that add up to an amazing package. The music is wonderfully composed, the graphics are clean and expressive, the story is well paced, the humor is done surprisingly well without mocking the serious objectives of the game, and the combat is fluid and exciting. Playing as a dragon is a cool concept if a bit underused, you can only do so in the last half of the original game and the last mission of the expansion. My only real complaint is the combat as a dragon. All you really fight are ballista towers and other dragons while in this mode. As such, you can't fight ground enemies as a dragon at all, so no chance to sweep some goblins with your fire breath. Even so, turning into a dragon in free fall more than makes up for this.
One thing in particular I liked was the mindreading mechanic. It opens up a whole slew of new posiblilites for you as a player as you try to decide which character would know something helplful to you. From rare items, stat bonuses, ability points, and all kinds of other little secrets, you'll find a much richer experience if you open your eyes and ears.
If you decide to pick this up, spring for the Directors cut like I did. Comes with the full game (which was tweaked from the original version), the expansion (which is really necessary to experience the story in full), Developer Mode (if you like to cheat like I do), and all kinds of extra bits like music from the whole divinity series, behind the scenes videos, and concept art. It's a total bargain for hours of the kind of quality RPG that you can just get lost in.

Each of the well-named citizens of your town (I'm talking to you, Tabitharitza!) will have some special significance to you, and you really want to help them prosper.  It is wonderful... for a time.

This was possibly the best $1.25 that I have ever spent. This game is a lot of fun and it has a lot of replayability. In addition to the seven maps in the main game, there are also many custom maps created by users that you can play through. My personal favorite level is the snow one. It is just a joy to play through.
In terms of gameplay, you basically roll a ball through beautiful and varied levels in order to reach an end goal and move on to the next. In addition to rolling, you are able to jump and use a power brake to instantly stop. Once you have beaten all the levels, you unlock ball designs inspired by each level and two new abilities you can use - teleport and double jump. There are timed leaderboards for each level and high scores for each of the minigames. Of the three minigames, the only one I returned to over and over was Crate Chaos because I was competing with someone for high scores.
I asked the person I played with if she wanted to add anything to this review and she said: This is a ♥♥♥♥ing awesome game. It is challenging without being too frustrating. I absolutely agree, but with that being said, I have to admit there were times when each of us rage quit out of frustration. That's the thing about this game - sometimes you might struggle with sections that seem ridiculously simple and other times you might breeze through them. There are absolutely challenging sections as well. There is an achievement for completing the seven main game maps in order without falling out once but I can't imagine ever dedicating the riduculous amount of time (and I'm going to say also luck) that it would take to accomplish that.
As for controls, I played throught this game once with the X-Box controller and once with the keyboard and mouse. What I found was that it was much easier to control my jump with the gamepad and easier to make tiny course adjustments with the keyboard/mouse. If you are struggling with one or the other, I suggest switching control schemes.
In short, this game was hours of fun for a very low price and it has the potential for tons of replayability. Especially if you were a beast at Marble Madness, you're probably going to want to check this out.

I will separate this into two categories: Single Player and Multiplayer. Seeing as both have different stories to tell, I feel it would be appropriate to split them up. Warning, there may be spoilers, but nothing that will ruin the whole story. Enjoy.
Single player:
The single player has a great story, as do most games made by Ubisoft. You start the story as Alex Taylor, a man and brother who gets put into prison and framed for his brothers' death, which was caused by the main antagonist, Shiv. Throughout the story, you compete and earn your rank through a sort of street gang lead by various characters by their status, (V2, V4, V6) ultimately trying to get to the top, V8, where Shiv stands.
Each city you unlock, which I might add are major cities throughout the United States, (LA, New York, Miami, etc.) you gain new members to your crew, or basically guidance and emotional support to your driving and discovery of locations, races and more. Your crew becomes a valuable asset to you, both becoming good friends and especially people you can count on.
Now, for the actual review part:
The single player had some good moments, great scenes, and overall a great racing experience. The handling of vehicles is the best I've seen throughout all my years of racing games, and takes the cake for that. The only thing I really wish they would have done was spend more time on the ending. It seemed very rushed and very anti-climactic. This though does not change my overall feel of the game, I still love it.
Multiplayer:
Multiplayer can be a separate story on its own simply in the fact you can basically go anywhere, with anyone. Traveling far distances with friends or strangers can be quite a great experience, especially if you can tolerate driving for literally hours at a time in real time. To put into perspective, you can probably make it across the whole map (let's say LA to Maine) in about an hour, or close to. This is driving at full speed, at least at 330km/h (at least I was).
There's plenty of places to visit, plenty of great atmospheric areas to go to. It can be very biased, but if you're not into driving for hours at a time, I wouldn't bother playing multiplayer, I'd just stick to the story.
All in all, it's a great game for what it's worth, can include hundreds of hours of multiplayer time if you're into it, or if not, you can free roam around at your will (and even go offroading in a dirt spec or raid vehicle!).

The Napoleon installment in the Total War franchise is, in my opinion, one of the best thus far. Compared to its predecessors, Napoleon TW boasts the best projectile combat for gunpowder based units (except for cannons). Line infantry, skirmishers, and snipers are all integrated effectively so that an armed comabt force can utilize all three of them without running into issues. Additionally, the balance of the game is quite good in that all units have counters and all counters have units that counter them. No one army can be used to defeat all counters. That being said, however, the game does have a few notable issues that detract from the enjoyability of the game. The first issue is that standard cannons have horrible trajectory algorithms. Cannons in Napoleon TW will consistently fire into the ground if they are not placed on flat ground or on a downward slope. This makes non-mortar artillery extremely frusterating to use since it is difficult to discern if the land you're deploying them on is 100% flat or if it is slightly rough. The second issue with the game is that melee combat is quite ackward due to a lack of proper unit collision in the game. As a result, units can be "pulled" through enemy lines by simply ordering units to run through the enemies. That being said, Napoleon TW is still a solid game and an excellent RTS. I recommend giving it a try.

I spent ~430 hours on battlefield 1, and only 4 hours on Verdun at the time of writing those lines.
Well.
I love Verdun much more than Battlefield 1 one on those points:
* Gameplay: targets are hard to see, and you're not a bullet-magnet like in BF1. You mean lifetime on the ground is much higher than with Bf1. Also when you die, you know exactly why: it's because of you, and only you. Not because the game let players shoot you 1 sec after you spawn.
* Weapons: they are so great. Iron sight is hard and painful, as it would be in reality. Controlling your weapon is a challenge. No matter what weapon it is: rifle, pistol, nades, anything…
* Maps: trenches, holes in the ground, dirt, trees, grass, barbed wires, forts, holly **** we're in it!
* Pace: slower than BF1, but you can "speed up" the thing by increasing field of view to 70-80. Still, the game is slower but offers a real challeng on the battlefield… see what i did there? hehe
* Technical performance: the game does run really good, much more than BF1 in low. (i7 6700K + GTX 970). And you still have good graphics that adds to the game. The environment gives you countless ways to hide, sneak under the wires and all.
* Game modes: frontlines, deathmatch, battle-against-waves-oh-i-forgot-the-name. In frontlines mode, you'll have to play with your team. And it's awesome!
* Weapon and class system: more complex than BF1, but has more to offer than, especially because weapons are really different. For example, you take the Lebel, you have 8 bullets. You take the Berthier, you have 3 DESTROYING bullets. But you cannot reload while your charger has bullets left inside.
What i dislike about the game, but doesn't matter that much to me:
* Graphics are "oldschool": a bit too grey and "rigid". But this is also a plus since it makes you dive in the war.
* Sound design: awww… it hurts. It wouldn't matter if it was only weapon sounds. It's the way sound is rendered in space and how you can use the sound to get information about your environment. In my opinion, it can be improved.
* UI: small fonts, too much things displayed and i have no idea what's it's for.  But you can enjoy the game without that :)
For those who like that, the game offers levels that you grow while playing in a squad, giving you bonus while playing. I'm not so interested with this part of the game, but a friend i play with really loves it.
This game can and should be improved, still i recommend this game for all those players who wants challenging game and immersion into war. Not just random shots in the head from campers at the other side of the map.

"Death is nothing; but to live defeated and inglorious is to die daily."
So the "Corsican Ogre" said. If the title didn't make it completely obvious, this game focuses on "The Little Corporal" and all the fun things he did from 1796 to 1815. Frankly I see this as a missed opportunity. Sure, Bonaparte is interesting and is perfectly capable of holding up a game by himself with how many military campaigns he did in his life, but this just as well could have been a game about the whole of the French Revolutionary period (back to 1789) and gotten more out of it. It is worth exploring the fact that Revolutionary France was already powerful and winning a war against almost all of Europe before Napoleon ever began his Italian campaign.
If you played any Total War game, and particularly Empire, you know what you are getting: Battles with dummy AI and a strategic map against an AI that is fond of stacking huge armies at the capital and leaving them there until you go kill them. The gameplay is almost identical to Empire's, but with more polish, a tighter focus, a horde of unique units all dressed up in the proper uniforms of the era, and a special series of campaigns. Basically there are two seperate campaigns here. There's the Coalition one which is basically like the typical grand campaign of the other Total War games, and then there's the Napoleon stuff that is much like the Road to Independence in Empire, but of a much better quality.
There are also lots of historical battles, and unlike alot of Total War games these ones are actually quite good. Most of the big ones of Napoleon's career: Lodi, Austerlitz, Borodino, Waterloo, and more are all here. There are a few important ones missing (Marengo, Leipzig), and you get two naval battles played as the French where, historically, the British absolutely trashed the French fleets (Aboukir Bay/Nile and Trafalgar). Trafalgar in particular is irritating, because you would think it would let you play as the British since it is probably Britain's most famous naval victory in history. Missed opportunity for a small and cheap Nelson DLC I think. They did make a free DLC where you can play as the British at Waterloo, which makes this Trafalgar omission all the more annoying. Oh well. On a positive note the historical battles are heavily scripted which, while making them predictable, also makes them pretty much just like they were historically. Nerds like me appreciate such things.
This game doesn't have the same large scale that other Total War games have, and that will annoy some. Ultimately, this game is for those interested in the Napoleonic Era. If you are such a person, then this game is a treat. Its AI problems are annoying, but they are no worse than other Total War games. I got alot of playtime out of this, and maybe you can too. :3

If you buy this game expecting a Red orchestra like experience, you will be disappointed.
This game is developed by a handful of guys and it shows. No disrespect to the hard work of the devs, but I cant in good concience recommend this game at full price. The gameplay tries to be a lethal one shot affair ala Red Orchestra in its bid to simulate trench warfare. However, the movement and weapon handling is incredibly clunky. This coupled with some lackluster meat grinder maps make for a very frustrating experience where tactics have very little impact on the gameplay.
There is also a very unfair level up system where the game only allows progress through playing with friends. There are TONS of perks to be unlocked, but these can ONLY be gained by leveling up a squad with people you played with before. Good luck if you play this game alone; you might be able to find a leveled up squad to join, but 90% of the time you will have to make your own or join a random squad without the level benefit. Why the devs thought this convoluted system of player progression was a good thing is beyond me. They have not made any attempts at changing it.
Furthermore, the classes in this game features some real weird loadouts. Some of them come equipped with only a spade and some grenades. Good luck if you are stuck in a squad where that class is the only option.
The good thing however is that this game is very impressive in terms of graphics. It looks incredibly realistic, and features historically correct equipment and uniforms. (However, you will not see most of these uniforms as they are unlocked as part of their "play with friends" progression system).
TL/DR: Clunky gameplay, no tactical options, unfair level progression, and very similar and lackluster map variety. Wait for a steam sale.

The news of Houston getting hit this morning shook me to the very core. I knew the Central American Theatre heated up after the Axis Powers invited Mexico into their faction with open arms but I didn't think it was this bad. Though i grew up in Amarillo, a town just a few hours away, i had fond memories of that city, and now i didn't even want to ponder on what it would look like with all of its buildings reduced to rubble and its clean streets littered with blast craters.
I let my mind linger on my home just a few measly miles from the front and what those Spanish b******* would really fight like if they weren't supplied with fresh panzers and small arms from Germany. I cut off those thoughts as not to distract me from what was hapenning now, and instead focused my thoughts on the bitter cold. Sitting in a foxhole with wet soil was bad enough, but the blisters on my hand from breaking apart the cement and digging what I thought might be my grave in the next few hours really stung in the brisk winter air. It sure was cold up North, we were hurried up here last week. I was in Sicily when the Krauts and what was left of the Italian army pushed us back out on the same path we blazed through the countryside. Operation Overlord was supposed to take some of the heat off of us but the krauts coastal defense gun fire was so heavy that the invasion never began. One of my long-time friends told me earlier in the week that the Germans used the same guns on their shores that we do, he has a history of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥tting so he's probably just pulling my leg.
A quick inspection of my M1 Garand appeased the creeping fear of any imperfection that could indanger its performance. My Garand truely is a weapon of beauty, just like The Old Man said, and sure beats those old Springfields that some poor old boys are being issued from stockpiles, but it can still seize up like any firearm. This here gun was by my side in North Africa, Sicily, Italy, and almost into Germant before they pushed us back. I've been hearing some talk around the company that a new rifle is being tested thats based off of those German paratrooper guns, the fallshrimp-whatcha-ma-call-them. I didn't care though, I liked my dusty old gun all the same.
I decided to stand up and stretch to get my blood flowing, some coffee would have been nice but the Army doesn't value us enough to prioritize its transportation. I looked around the dark city street that was just being illuminated by the rising sun. These tall buildings weren't unheard of around Amarillo, h***, Houston "had" some but they were easily dwarfed by these monstrosities. A glimmer of light revealed the big red "1" on my shoulder as i turned to face the harbor. It normally would have been a breathtaking sight if it wasn't for the silhouettes of 6 H-class battleships with support vessels looming like a storm cloud. Just staring at them made me nervous. They decimated our 5th fleet 2 weeks ago, it was our last Atlantic fleet. A sigh escaped my lips as i sat back down to check on the M2 and wake my friend Joe. Joe was from these parts and on our rare walks around the city he'd recount memories from his childhood and old spots he spent with 5 of the loves of his life, supposedly each one hotter than the last. I shook him awake and he retorted with an irratable "whaddya want, tough guy?". I always told him he talked funny and he always countered with a "Can it, cowboy", new additions to our unit always assumed we hated each other but thats just how best friends joke, we refused to turn to that dark humor the other guys resorted to.
He dug into his pocket and hand with 2 sticks of gum. Tossing one to me, he asked if anything new sprung up. I didn't wish to go back to my pessimistic thoughts of home so i just told him that things were quiet. Our daily conversation of "which babe is better" or "how far do you think I can hit this-or-that" began as if it to was apart of our routine, if you can count sitting on your♥♥♥♥♥all day in the name of freedom a routine.
After roughly 45 minutes of chatting we quited back down. I decided to return to my Playboy magazine as he started scrubbing his rifle.
"I swear man, as the war drags on, these women, get uglier."
"Yeah, that's because the Jerry's got all the nice broads."
"I guess so....hey man can you stop humming?"
"What? I was 'bout to ask you the same thing."
"Well one of us has got to cut it out."
"Stop lying man you stupid son of a-"
KAPOW
As a wave of dust washed over us, an air raid siren began to wail. I rocked the charging handle on the M2 and fixed it on the harbor, as i scanned the horizon i noticed something new. Dozens of tiny dots were slowly getting closer.
They were landing craft.
The Battle of New York was beginning.

I really wanted to and tried to like this game because it is part of the Divinity series but its just fails to be entertaining or worthwhile. It's an ARPG with bad and sloppy combat, and the majority of gameplay is endless tedious trudging through generic cartoonish uninteresting MMO themepark landscapes that suffer from invisible wall syndrome. The dragon flight mode is a painful chore. At times the quest system and narrative does a completely inadequate job at explaining things and not in a good way.
Maybe the console version was more responsive, but there's no native controller support on PC. That might be acceptable for an action-oriented title of its age if it's mouse/keyboard control weren't so sloppy. It's just not responsive enough for an action RPG, and even using it with the Steam Controller cannot fix the underlying problems. It doesn't work as an action title and there's not enough meat on the bones for it to stand alone as an RPG.
There is some good to be said about it which is why I tried to stick with it so long. It has really compelling and polished weapon, armor, magic and skill progression and loot systems. A game built around those alone could be really good. Too bad they feel completely wasted on the rest of this game. Voice acting and music is passable, and there are some really good ideas such as being able to build a companion creature out of parts, and the staff of various servants at your base.
The generic writing and quests might have been adequate enough if the game held up as an action title with decent combat, but at least on PC it does not, leaving no real reason to keep playing.

Refunct is a short little game about the pure joys of first-person traversal in a beautiful, ever-changing landscape of pillars and water.  The goal of the game is to use your acrobatic abilities to reach red buttons that when stepped on, cause new pillars to shoot out of the ocean and add further complexity to your surroundings.  Calming techno music plays in the background while your character effortlessly navigates this surreal setting of endless ocean and setting suns with grace and fluidity; jumping off of walls and climbing ledges with pleasingly little hassle.
As each pillar platform is stepped upon, it changes from a cold, stone slab to earth and grass.  You literally leave your mark on the world and grow its intricacies out as you progress; making your playground bigger and prettier with each little victory.  It gives the game a journey and driving force that is distilled down to the simplest of acts, almost like a gardener tending his land.  You get caught up in it and before you know it, you've finished the game in a single sitting, which only takes about 30 minutes. A great game that really suprised me! It plays like a WWI game should-- trying to run around in the open and get "epic" moments gets you shot. Sitting up in a trench gets you shot. Poking your rifle through cover or a hole in in some sandbags gets you killed. Grenades hurt. Smoke grenades are practical.
Perhaps the best thing-Nobody has an automatic rifle, unlike another popular WWI shooter.... Over 90% of players have bolt action rifles. Those with semi-automatic machine guns are a force to be reckoned with. One shot is enough to kill or get killed in nearly every situation. No wacky vehicles are in the game, like huge airships, trains, planes, or god forbid, tanks. The infantry gun play is the primary focus and is super enjoyable-if you play the game right! Being a jackass and running around by yourself trying to capture a trench on the opposite side of the map will result in many, many deaths.
The battlefields/objectives are clear. No mans land, the area between trenches is not a fun place to be. Working with your team to clear the trenches is great fun. Great blend of tactical/casual play. Verdun is one of the few games I keep installed on my HDD, and I'd love to sink more time into it soon.

Never thought I'd be a Souls fan. Dark Souls II blew my mind and changed my world, and Scholar of the First Sin is an amazingly seamless addition to an already overwhelmingly addicting game.
Even experiencing Dark Souls III afterwards, the solid build quality and crispness of everything from animations to controller responsiveness in the second Souls game keeps me whipped. The storyline and lore backing it up might as well be a series of encyclopedias, as the game itself won't even cover about 60% of it, and it makes you work to discover even the smallest snippets of some of the history of the lands, characters, weapons... only intriguing you to venture further into the (ridiculously) unforgiving environment to unveil both answers and more questions. Combat is invigorating and high-risk-high-reward, punishing even the slightest delay in reaction time or poorly-timed attacks. Relief is tangible when finally finding one of the sparse bonfires, or slaying even a miniboss; you will soon learn, anything and everything will ♥♥♥♥ you up in this game in 3 seconds or less. On the upside, you have a selection of about 350 swords, shields, axes, staffs, lances, hammers, etc available to you to hack, smash, slice, stab, and generally ♥♥♥♥ up anything within a 20ft radius, along with a similar number of armor pieces to make sure you're protected and/or stylish.
PVP? Surprisingly still somewhat active, but make sure to read into level caps for matchmaking, or deal with dueling extreme high-level builds that rely less on skill as much as spam.
Tl;dr If you're interested in constantly walking around with a random melee weapon, often alone, in some desolate land that wants you dead, populated exclusively with creatures that want to slaughter you, hop aboard the Souls train.

Having finally gotten over the steep learning curve (made a lot faster by watching Michael Broschek's tutorials), I can say this game is a lot easier than it looks at first glance. Similar to Dwarf Fortress, when I first started playing, it looked to be an impermeable mess of menus and overcomplicated gibberish, but once you finally dove in (perhaps after watching a let's play or the tutorials as I mentioned above), everything slowly pieces itself together.
The first game you play, you can expect to make a TON of mistakes, but after your first playthrough, everything should start becoming more natural to you, and you'll improve with every subsequent playthrough (learning where to focus first, what your strategy should be, how to actually use the AI for handling theatres, and so on).
For anyone who is looking for a very in-depth grand strategy experience, I'd say look no further than Hearts of Iron 3 (although I do suggest you try out Paraodox's easier grand strategy games like Europa Universalis IV and Crusader Kings 2 to acclimate yourself to the engine). Every country in the world that exists during this time period is playable (although good luck as El Salvador...), and you aren't limited to just the major powers.
However, if you do pick up Hearts of Iron 3, I highly suggest getting all of the expansions with it, as well as using large address aware (LAA) on the game's .exe (the lack of LAA practically broke the game on my system).

Refunct is a short little game about the pure joys of first-person traversal in a beautiful, ever-changing landscape of pillars and water.  The goal of the game is to use your acrobatic abilities to reach red buttons that when stepped on, cause new pillars to shoot out of the ocean and add further complexity to your surroundings.  Calming techno music plays in the background while your character effortlessly navigates this surreal setting of endless ocean and setting suns with grace and fluidity; jumping off of walls and climbing ledges with pleasingly little hassle.
As each pillar platform is stepped upon, it changes from a cold, stone slab to earth and grass.  You literally leave your mark on the world and grow its intricacies out as you progress; making your playground bigger and prettier with each little victory.  It gives the game a journey and driving force that is distilled down to the simplest of acts, almost like a gardener tending his land.  You get caught up in it and before you know it, you've finished the game in a single sitting, which only takes about 30 minutes.  A fittingly short journey for a simple but effective concept, and a ton of fun while it lasts.

I played this game first time in 2011-2012 and I replayed it in 2017.
What can I tell you about this game? I love it!
The RPGs from Larian Studio are always have some unique features and interesting characters.
In this game:
1.	You can explore a vast open world. It is not as big as worlds from Bethesda (like Skyrim / Fallout) but it is pretty big. There are many places to go and things to see.
2.	You can read other people minds. Sometimes it can be fun, sometimes it can provide you with some lore about world, experience points or skill points.
3.	You have your own undead pet – a pretty useful companion. You can find different body parts for your pet and customize it with the help of a necromancer.
4.	You have your own Battle tower with several subordinates who can help you with necromancy, blacksmithing or alchemy.
5.	You have plenty skills for use – from conjuring spirits to rush attacks with your swords.
6.	You will find dozens (if not hundreds) of puzzles and secrets. Even in the training area a sharp-sighted player can find something interesting! And most of the times the game will not give you any direct hints (like flags on the map), so you actually need to carefully read texts and look for hints. Do yourself a favor – don’t use any online guides unless you completely stuck.
7.	You can transform into a dragon!
8.	There are dozens and dozens of quests, especially in the second part.
9.	There are plenty interesting NPC, I bet you won’t forget Bellegar )
10.	And many other things …
Of course, it is not an ideal game.
There are some flaws in combat system and using the dragon form can be boring sometimes, but all these little things weren’t able to spoil my fun.
As I said before – I love this game. It is very distinctive from other RPGs and for me it is one of the most important feature in games.

A very challenging, unforgiving game in which you must pause, plan and prioritize your town's structures and workforce. You begin with only a handful of people and supplies, gathering resources from the land around you. Your objective is to build a thriving, bustling town of people, all the while avoiding major issues such as work-related deaths, possible disease outbreaks, overpopulation, resource scarcity and weather disasters (if you prefer to play with a harsh climate). If you manage to prevent all of these disasters from occurring, you must then brace yourself and your banished villagers for the possibility of starvation and/or freezing to death. And if you're finally able to brave all of these conditions and make it out alive...
...you get to start the second year! :)

I was gladly surprised by how much I enjoyed this experience. It was gentle, peaceful (for the most part), and for me personally, nostalgic - in way both good and bad. The life of the protagonist was obviously difficult, but not without joy. I image them growing up to be an astronomer or electrician just as the game hinted they would. The narration was also very believable and nicely done. I continually found new things on following playthroughs that even kept it interesting past the developers intended playtime. (Apparently people are speed-running it... somehow).
I have always had a bit of a love-hate relationship with walking sims. I either adore them and their slow method of storytelling (as I did Rapture) or despise them (sorry folks, it was a great experience for some, I'm sure, but Dear Esther just didn't do it for me.) This one however was long enough to draw me in and I honestly wanted to see more of the young protagonists life and memory. This was kind of a flaw for me in that I would've loved to have more and the ending felt somewhat abrupt. I wonder how much of the game was inspired by experiences the developer had as a child - I can't image where else certain things in the game came from.
There are a few glitches that could use work - I occasionally walked through scenery, the game occasionally crashed, and appears to freeze when attempting to close, but this could be to do with my only being able to play on PC, and not owning an Oculus. I imagine that would not have such a problem.

This is a great game for many reasons. I shall list some of them in the following areas of this review.
Gameplay: You will connect people from a corrupt government to a gas canister, shoot said gas canister and murder more corrupt men whilst watching the aforementioned gas canister fly everywhere. 9.5/10
Graphics: This game was released in 2010 and it easily looks plenty better than a lot of modern games. It also runs very well but I shall get on to that later. 9/10
Open World: Now, you may have heard that this game is open world in which case the source was correct. The aforementioned open world spans 923km² and is packed with a LOT to do. It is also very fun to travel in as there are many cars, motorbikes, boats, trucks, helicopters, jets, old-style planes and even your parachute and grapple that are in your disposal. For context, GTAV is 256km² and The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim is 37.1km². Think about that for a second. 10/10
Performance: I shall only tell you the essential parts of my rig right now but just remember, even if you have the parts that I am going to list, your mileage may vary. I have a NVIDIA PALiT GeForce GTX 760 with 2GB of GDDR5 VRAM, an intel i7-4770K (whatever it was clocked to in the factory, I was too lazy to check) and 16GB of Kingston RAM, I also am forced to use V-Sync as my monitor is TERRIBLE with screen tearing and runs at 60Hz. I can easily run this game on ultra but I do have to sacrifice SOME frames, I usually like to put it on high and just do a little bit of tweaking around with the settings just to be sure but it is NOT difficult to maintain 60fps in this game, even on the higher settings. I am just significantly paranoid because I saw a comparison between the 760 and 980, you don't need a monster rig, arguably I have one, to run this game even though it looks better than most modern games. It is also 10GB, think about that, CS: GO is 8GB. It is amazing that it has such good texture quality in such a BIG game at that low hard drive space (or SSD space). Now, sadly the loading times aren't that great (keep in mind that I am running it on a HDD which I may change soon) but it's not like Watch_Dogs or Deus Ex: Human Revolution (on launch). 9/10
Verdict: From the looks of it, you may be able to tell that I like this game. That is because I do. As this is the case, I give it a stellar 9.5/10. It is a great game and you can also get it with the first (if you want it) by getting the Just Cause Collection. It is worth every penny you spend on it and should bring you great joy if you like the genre. Remember, the verdict is 9.5/10.

I don't mind short games. Not anymore, at least. And I don't mind walking simulators. There are some good ones out there like The Stanley Parable... and the Stanley Parable... and did I mention the Stanley Parable?
Home Is Where One Starts tells the story of a girl returning to an old trailer that she lived in with a drunk father, and you get to explore the area that she once lived in, as she recounts of her memories there. Under normal circumstances, this seems just like the kind of game I'd like, isn't it?
But these aren't normal circumstances.
First off, the world you visit, while pretty to look at is very stale after a while. There's only a handful of interactive items interspersed in this world that you can find, and actually finding them seems more like a chore, as the dog food and flask seemed more like a game of a scavenger hunt, but I wasn't promised a prize at the end.
Along with that, there really isn't anything unique to learn about the girl. Her dad was an abusive drunk, she liked space, and she liked to live out on her own, to create space from her father. Beyond that, she mentions little to nothing of her neighbors, her friends from school, her friends from out of school, her mother, her other relatives, the relationship her parents had. For a world she lived in, there aren't a lot of memories to be stimulated. Just a lot of things to look at with her voiceover telling you their significance.
If this game looks like the sort of artistic walking simulator that will whet your appetite, then by all means buy it. I'm sure you'd get more entertainment from it that I did. But I'm, unfortunately, giving this one a 5/10. I actually did want to like this game, but the lack of complexity or uniqueness makes this an ultimately forgettable experience.

I saw Victor Vran when it arrived on steam. Added it to wishlist. However, I didn't buy it but got V. Vran from Humble Bundle. I couldn't find enough time to play but I see Victor Vran is shorter than Diablo 3, Van Helsing and Torchlight. I beat the game within 6.5 hours only.
Victor Vran is surprisingly good. I did expect this game to be good but this is a very well made game. Developers are the Tropico's dev team. Tropico and Victor Vran? Didn't match huh? Well don't feel awkward cuz they did the job. Victor Vran is an ARPG game. Isometric playstyle, Hack and Slash mechanics (also some shooting) and the most important this is an indie game. You simply kill, demolish/destroy or blow up your enemies. Then loot, then complete your quest, level up et cetera. Classic isometric rpg as you can understand. I'd like to say the story is quite interesting from the beginning.
STORY (7/10) :
You are an old prince who uses a power and made a deal with demons (like Ghost Rider but thanks god you still look stylish) and messed up. You have an unknown voice in your head. That voice make (always) joke on you. That voice also does some joke about movies/games (kind of easter egg). I won't tell you who is the voice (no spoiler !). However it's a quite good narrator and funny.
As i said, Victor Vran was a stylish guy. But he messed up. His land and people paid a price like famine. He had to move on and sort of escape. Also he is looking for a friend called Adrian. Adrian is last located in Zagoravia. Victor Vran travels to Zagoravia, becomes a hunter... Then he finds out that his friends gone crazy and turned (not like a zombie). Victor Vran decides to stay in Zagoravia, fight with evil force of demon realm, help the Queen. The rest is pretty cliche actually.
Victor finds out about Queen's deal and Zagoravia's fate. Then he meets with a old ghost. He travels into the demon's realm. Meets a guy which is the main villain and most likely douch-ebag (also it's not hard to guess. Main villain is not that superb), kills him and saves the Zagoravia for a while...

Also you do look really stylish as hunter Victor. Costumes are really good looking. Other characters also looks good and have some nice quotes.
GAMEPLAY (8/10) :
Well, you can jump. You can actually jump. I jumped when i am in a labyrinth. I jumped from a height. That's actually awesome for a Izometric ARPG. Rolling mechanic works good. There is some different weapons ; melee ones are Sword,Hammer,Scythe, Rapier. Hack and slash mechanis are enjoyable. Shooting mechanics are a bit 'meh' but it is good at overall. You can use a gun or Lighting Gun (that's my favourite). Lighting Gun is awfully enjoyable to use.
There is some unusual weapons aswell ; Lightsaber and Rainbow gun for example. I couldn't get them but i can say they looks pretty awesome (i watched the videos). The amount of weapon type is not that much but still fair enough.
There is various types of enemies. The champions are mostly same with the normal creatures and they just have better damage,health or some special effects. Boss fights are incredibly well but there is a two spider boss fight and the first and the final boss are a bit same. I did expect more creative boss fights when I saw the Adrian boss fight but it is okay. They are challenging and kind of unique.
You can select rewards when you got leveled up. It can be a random reward, destiny card, some unique rune (i'll call them rune, they just simply are. You can use them for your weapon/armor), armor/weapon, a special demon power etc.
Destiny cards gives you some special effects and advantages (like frost attack to enemies, health or extra armor). You can equip a demon power which is extremely strong. Weapons have alignment ; Common/Uncommon/Rare/Ultra Rare and Legendary. (It doesn't say that is ultra rare or not but you can understand from the colors. Green is always common, blue is rare, orange is better and in this one purple is the most good one the legendary one.)
Armors does have some advantages and all of them looks so good.
You can upgrade your weapon simply forging 3 same kind of weapon together. Also you can use your runes at them. It unlocks at level 16.
You probably won't get a problem with amount of potion. Potions are highly usable and they have recharge time. So you can not spam a health potion :)
Inventory is easy to use. There is no side quests really but high amount of challanges. Another thing is there is some extra boss fights and levels. I've finished the game in one day. Played 6 hours and around thirty min. I can say this is not a speedrun at all. The game is quite short and easy (i don't know it's just me, it says 12 hours on howlongtobeat). If you are not used to play games like this play the game on easy mode. It is really easy. On normal, it's fair enough. You can still beat within 6-8 hours. I've explored some ares, got 22 level and finished the game. Worth the money but it is short. I haven't complete all of the ares and challanges tho. Optional things can extend the playtime to around 12-16 hrs.

Level Design (9/10) :

Hell yeah. That's the level design i was looking for. City level, forest level, hell/demon realm level. It's all detailed and colors are matched up great. Well my eyes usually got rotten because the levels are too detailed and there is a lot of mobs (creatures) and they do some speels, i also do some spells... It's a total chaos. But level design and creature design is so decent. Just makes my eyes tried (my eyes are a bit bad, may be that's why).
Hah and you can control the camera. I nearly forgot to say that.
Graphics (8.5/10) :
Graphics are decent aswell as like Level Design. Damn good art style. The performance of game is pretty good. I've got 60 fps on high settings (gtx970, others are written in my profile page). Got 30fps on ultra settings. It's fair enough but i got some fps drops on high when there is a lot of creature and animations like spell casting, special powers etc.
Nothing more to talk. Graphics are fine by me. Since this is a indie ARPG, i am okay with these graphics. It looks like 2014-2015 graphics and that's a good thing. Matches up with current gen.
SCORE : 80/100
Totally worth it. This is kind of subjective review but I did try to do my best. At least get this from sale and there is a upcoming Summer Sale.

Voice Casting and OST :
May I say Geralt? Geralt of Rivia's voice actor Doug in this game. The voice really remembered me Geralt. It actually similar as Geralt. I nearly can say Victor Vran is Geralt of Rivia, lol. He did a great job again with that voice. If you ever played Witcher at least for once, you will understand what I mean. His voice is awesome among others like Adam Jensen, Lara Croft, Nathan Drake. As Victor Vran, I never get bored from that voice. (AWKWARD SENTENCE AGAIN) The other Voice's voice is sounds good and cheerful. The rest are not silly so it's okay.
OST and Soundtrack is quite good but everyone has a different taste, yeah? If I talk with my taste, it is fine. You can always listen it from youtube tho. But I recommend soundtrack and artbook content. Support to the devs!
Special thanks for Turkish localization. I did try it and one of the most professional localization i've ever seen.
PS : About easter eggs ; there is GebaN (GabeN) and achievement called 'Steamed out'. The voice says a quote which is 'I am your father !. Nooooo!.' That's a star wars easter egg. There is a lot of easter egg about Van Helsing, Gangnam Style, TES Skyrim (arrow in the knee thing. again.) etc.

[ENG] Very very enjoyed this third amazing chapter. I indeed played the two prequels, and this time something has changed. First of all we can notice that it has been introduced the same achievement system from Fairy Fencer (ps: you really should play it if you enjoyed Hyperdimension Neptunia <3), basically these are small tasks that the more you complete, the more they'll give you small bonuses. (Example: You jump 100 times you'll get extra 10 STR, 1000 times 15 STR etc. etc.). These tasks aren't so important, also each character has its own achievements.
Another important change is the Exe Drive Gauge that has been removed. In other words, the Exe Drive Gauge has been included in the SP (basically the Mana) bar. So your SP bar is not used just for casting normal spells, the more you'll fill it the more you'll able to use your different Combo finishers as well as your EXE skills. (Combo finishers won't consume SP bar, it just require it filled by a certain amount, while the EXE and normal skills consume it).
Despite that i refused to play with Histoire since i found her way too op (same for the new character in late game).
Last minor change is about endings, don't worry no spoilers. You finally don't have to end a game every time with different % Nation's shares :D. However the true ending requires a lot of grinding, but if you manage to get it... just worth it. Best ending of all Neptunia series.
Oh almost forgot the most important part of the review: Yes, the plot is even more amazing with even new more amazing characters. The gameplay is more or less still the same, but it's just so good anyway :3
If you enjoyed playing all the prequels then you definitely can not miss this awesome chapter, JUST GET IT <3

[ITA] Mi è davvero piaciuto tanto tanto questo terzo capitolo. Ho giocato indubbiamente i due prequel, e questa volta troviamo delle differenze. Innanzitutto possiamo notare come è stato introdotto il sistema di achievement identico a Fairy Fencer (ps: dovreste giocarlo se vi è piaciuta la saga di Neptunia!), in pratica consiste in piccole missioni che più vengono completate e più daranno bonus aggiuntivi permanenti. (Per esempio: Saltare 100 volte con un personaggio vi darà automaticamente 10 punti forza, saltare 1000 volte ve ne darà 15 e così via). Queste piccole missioni non sono di così fondamentale importanza, inoltre ogni personaggio ha le sue proprie missioni, quindi se proprio vorreste massimizzarvi un personaggio con tutti i bonus possibili dovreste sbloccare gli stessi achievement PER OGNI personaggio, e fidatevi che sono troppi.
Un altro cambiamento importante è la barra EXE (Exe Drive Gauge) che è stata rimossa, o meglio, integrata con la barra SP (praticamente il Mana). In parole semplici, la barra SP non servirà più solamente per evocare le magie normali, ma avrà anche la funzione di permettere l'uso della Combo Finisher (ovvero l'attacco base finale, normalmente il 4° attacco del personaggio di tipo Rush, Power o Break) quando si avrà la barra riempita di una certa quantità (in base a quanto richiede la Combo Finisher). Inoltre le skill finali EXE consumeranno semplicemente la barra SP esattamente come le skill normali.
A parte questi cambiamenti, mi sono rifiutato di giocare con Histoire in squadre perchè secondo me è troppo OP (così come il nuovo personaggio giocabile verso la fine del gioco).
Un altro piccolo cambiamento, tranquilli niente spoiler, finalmente non dovrete più scervellarvi a ottenere i finali basati sulla % degli share di ogni nazione :D. Nonostante ciò, il true ending (tanto per cambiare) richiede tanto grinding, ma se riuscirete ad ottenerlo... beh, sappiate che secondo me è stato il miglior finale di tutta la saga, davvero fantastico <3.
Oh quasi dimenticavo la parte più importante della recensione: SI, la trama è fantastica con personaggi altrettanto fantastici! Ormai sappiamo che il gameplay alla fine è lo stesso, ma è tutto troppo bello comunque :3
Se vi sono piaciuti i due sequel, allora non potete assolutamente perdervi questo terzo bellissimo capitolo.

I love this game. It's the first that stopped me from playing/modding elder scrolls completly until finished since BioShock Infinte. It's a typical old-school RPG, but a damn good one. I don't think it's really hard, nor easy. Seems just about the right difficualty too me. It has a nice storyline, the kind of humour I love from RPGs (like the guy who's SoulForced with a chicken, or the ability to spread pretty bad rumours) and gives some unique features like mind reading and becoming a dragon. It's somewhat old but it does still work well gameplay wise.
I havn't had any problem with balancing. Regen starts slow, but the game is pretty easy at that point, and with the right armours and skills it can become quite fast (I never used potions during this game, I just jump arround until my health is refilled). Just like in elder scrolls, it's possible to mix and match all RPG classes, so you're not limited to warrior, rogue or mage. After you have become a dragon, you will be able to reset your skills (at that point it costed me at most 10% of my in-game money, pretty cheap, but price will go up every time you do it), so little misstakes and skills you tried but didn't like can easily be fixed. There is indeed no respawn in this game, so limited gold an XP, but I managed to stay overleveld during the game. I defiantly got more gold and XP then needed and also have been able to beat places that where 5 levels above mine, so it's not really a problem. I actually think you'll become overleveld easily if respawning would be included.
The only downsides I have is that the in-game AA doesn't work (like there is an option but it doesn't do anything), and that shadows on characters are horribly blocky (but environment is great). Turned shadows off and made some Re-Shade preset (which I also gave some Ambient Occlusion to fake shadows) and it looks quite decent, considering it's release date.
Next to that the game has an issues with newer(mainly faster) hardware. It will tear on 60FPS (because my hardware is rendering faster then the engine can handle). Capping the game at 30 easily fixed the problem and makes the game look smooth again. Otherwise I haven't found any issues on performance (running Windows10, gtx1080 (2000+MHz), i5-6600K (4.2GHz), 16GB DDR4).
Also the autosave is horrible. It only saves before some plot parts for main storyline. If you die you will have to reload a save, so it would be good to get used to saving manually often.
Still, my biggest archievement in this game is when I find some pants that have good stats for my level, because Larian loves miniskirts it seems. Just makes me think someone forgot to put on her pants/leg protection in the morning.

Good voice-acting. Female NPCs with pretty faces. Watch your player character in underwear, if you take off every piece of armor. The background music doesn't match the atmosphere always.
I've enjoyed the initial exploration in a rather restricted area (aka "Broken Valley") that seemed interesting enough. And I've enjoyed the blind flight, because I was playing carefully and without following any guides or walkthroughs.
Then I've struggled during the second half. Tedious, dull, repetitive drudgery to attempt a completionist playthrough in order to be able to reach high levels. And even then the experience points mechanics require a variety of special tricks to turn in quest XP at the right time and kill enemies in the right order for more XP. Nevertheless, eventually I almost felt over-powered due to the high level and access to tons of special equipment. The occasional balancing issues made a very few minor boss fights unexpectedly difficult, and I assure you, there are players, who "rage quit" the game in such a situation. You can always search for help or hints, but be prepared to find unhelpful comments from either braggarts, or from people, who only know the older release of this game.
Haven't run into crashes or obvious bugs. Except in the heat of combat, sometimes either my mouse stopped accepting camera rotation input. Or music stopped playing. Quicksave and quickload fixed it directly during combat.
And finally, I've run into a game-breaking bug that is known for years, unfortunately. It's been discussed before. I've mentioned it in the forum, too, before writing this review. An enemy four levels below me, who kills me either with the first magic attack I cannot avoid or with the next attack a second later. There are videos, where that doesn't happen. There are players, who play the game with half the health points and with many more wasted skill points. But there are reports that describe exactly the same problem that can cause real frustration.
It seems, the players of this edition of the game are supposed to fire up the game in the separate developer mode and activate a cheat mode to work around that problem. Not sexy at all.
Edit #1: A bit later, the same bug apparently also affected another important fight and made it almost impossible even with lots of cheat modes activated. Enemies moved too quickly and were much too resistant to damage to stop them as required during that fight where they approach from three directions and respawn, too. Again, when searching the web about it, I see the same reports by other players and also videos where the enemies move much slower and can be eliminated with ease. Here it seemed impossible even with godlike cheats, multiple summons and holding down the key to launch magical area attacks all the time. Whatever it is that messed up my game on "Normal" difficulty so late, it's the opposite of fun.
Edit #2: In the end, I've decided not to turn off the cheat modes anymore for the final fight. The frustrating experience has been too much of a motivation killer, and I've also decided against continueing into the add-on due to this.

Despite a pretty failed launch the game has been improved over time and now the driving physics are actually decent.
However, getting air and other "bumpy" actions tends to still be very flawed and unpredictable.

The main downfall is there are still quite a few bugs and multiplayer matchmaking only works sometimes. I often end up spending either a few minutes to find a crew to do the crew challenge at Summit events or more often than not the matchmaker never seems to find someone else for even hours. Physics when on rough terrain (Raid and Monster Trucks usually) tend to be very unpredictable and frustrating.
Another flaw is there is basically no competitive reason to turn off assists and use manual gear shifting as even when manual the cars shift rather slow. There may be a slight advantage to using sport mode instead of full assits though its only minor as the steering assist sometimes does drive a player off course and that is reduced in sport. Contrary to most other driving games there is no acceleration penalty when using full assistance and automatic gearing.

If you think you're good at management sims, you should step up and try Banished. It will humble you. Unless you do everything right and provide for about 17 different needs for all your people at all times without fail or delay, people are going to die. A lot of people. The game's resource generation vs consumption is incredibly tilted against you. Unless you have fully educated villagers using the best tools and wearing the warmest clothing and in exactly just the right amount of houses (not too few, not too many), it's a long slow slide into starvation and desperation. My village has been going about 43 years, but because villagers apparently age at 4 times the normal rate (I started off with 10 villagers in their 20s, and within 5 years the oldest ones in the village were in their 40s easy) there have been generations of turnover, especially due to all the starvation. You can't farm enough. You can't forage enough. You can't mine enough, you can't quarry or herd or smith or log enough, fast enough. At my peak, my village boasted almost 100 residents. After about a 20 year recession that worsened into depression (not helped by the frequently completely useless merchants that came to call, no I don't want to buy your stupid pumpkin seeds, I already grow my own, why the hell didn't you bring iron), I'm back under 30 residents, mostly from starvation.
The game plays very similar to Tropico or Gnomoria in that instead of controlling individual villagers you simply order the places for them to live and work built, and manage as a taskmaster/city planner. It starts off kind of easy because a new map will have abundant resources just lying on the ground around you... but once you use that up, it's much slower and more expensive to mine it/cultivate it/quarry it. There are no goblin attacks, no rebels, no hurricanes or zombies... just your silent mental wail as you watch people under your charge wither and die because your skills at management were a single iota less than divinely perfect.
This game is nice to play and is one of my favourite games.

From the look of it, this game is called the "80's Shoot'Em Up Kit" so chances are Retro Space Shooter is something else. What is it to me though? Well to me it was two levels and a whole three or four minutes to complete the "game."
For anyone looking for a real review, this is a tough one. Do I critique the "game" or do I talk about the "kit?"
As a game, the trailer feels misleading as a lot of what's in the trailer isn't in the game, but let's talk about what is here. There are debugging options always on screen you can click on to enable coins, invulnerability and a debug mode. Its a bit silly to leave them in here in a game, but when you're flipping the "80's Shoot'Em Up Kit" onto Steam, why take the time to remove them?
Killing rows of enemies gives you item pickups that result in better weapons such as bombs that fall down and a dual shot that fires up at an angle. The weapons are meaningless when the "game" is so short before it loops. A game this short would benefit from having a high score, let alone leaderboard support.
If you're here for a game, then you should avoid Retro Space Shooter. If your game is more of a witch hunt, then this is right up your alley, so I'd recommend getting your tomatoes!
